chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi Al-Razzaz narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Bashir al-Sarraj, from Abu Sa'id al-Qadi, who said:

I entered the chamber of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and found Murazim with him. I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on foot, Allah will record for him, with every step and with every foot he raises and places, the freeing of a slave from the children of Ismail. And whoever visits him by ship, if their ship carries them, a caller from the heavens will call out to them: 'Be delighted, and Paradise will be pleasing to you.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific rewards for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn on foot or by ship?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition highlighting the immense spiritual merit of physically traveling to Imam al-Husayn’s shrine, emphasizing the tangible rewards for pilgrimage efforts. The distinction between walking and traveling by sea underscores the accessibility of this reward across different modes of transport, while the celestial announcement for sea travelers reflects the unique status of Karbala as a focal point of divine mercy and intercession in Shia devotional practice.
